key_insight: The paper shows how to control false alarms when screening documents for AI-generated text, even when the detector can adaptively choose which parts of a document to inspect. It provides two finite-sample conformal constructions that remain valid without assuming independence between tokens inside a document.
problem_solved: AI-text screening often needs to inspect only part of a document and may adapt its decisions as evidence accumulates, but this can make false-alert control difficult. The paper addresses how to keep screening reliable when the procedure can stop early and when text within a document is highly dependent.
method: Uses document-level exchangeability between calibration documents and a new null document to guarantee finite-sample validity.
Builds adaptive within-document screening procedures that can select prefixes and detectors from observed evidence.
Introduces two conformal constructions that control false alerts while allowing early stopping before the full inspection budget is used.
impact: This matters for practitioners who need trustworthy AI-text detectors in real settings such as moderation, compliance, or provenance checking. It offers a principled way to reduce false positives while still enabling efficient, adaptive inspection.
visual_elements: A flow diagram showing calibration documents, a new document, prefix selection, detector choice, and stopping rule
A side-by-side comparison of non-adaptive vs adaptive screening workflows
A false-alert control chart illustrating guaranteed error control under finite samples
An infographic of a document being scanned prefix-by-prefix with an early-stop marker
paper_title: Two Conformal Constructions for Adaptive Within-Document AI-Text Screening
paper_authors: Marco Mandap, Jerahmeel Hipolito, Arcel Galvez, Charlie Margaret Balagtas, Michael Joshua Buluran
